universities.name: University of Novi Sad Faculty of Medicine
universities.summary: University of Novi Sad Faculty of Medicine has taught medicine since 1960 and has run its English-medium Medicine track since 1993, offering a direct-entry, six-year MD programme listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG eligibility from 1963 onward. Its accreditor, Serbia's National Accreditation Body, most recently confirmed the study programme's accredited status in November 2020.
universities.campusLifestyle: The English-track Medicine programme is a smaller, intake-limited cohort -- 15 seats for Medicine in the 2026/27 September admission term -- supported by an International Department and Erasmus Student Network volunteers who help incoming international students settle in.
universities.cityProfile: Novi Sad is Serbia's second-largest city, on the Danube river in the Vojvodina region. The Faculty's primary teaching hospital, the Clinical Center of Vojvodina, has served as its main clinical and research base since the 1960s-70s.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS integrated Medicine programme (first- and second-level studies combined, leading directly to the Doctor of Medicine title) is taught entirely in English. Clinical training runs through the Clinical Center of Vojvodina, the Faculty's principal teaching hospital since its clinical-hospital status was formalized in the 1960s-70s. A detailed year-by-year pre-clinical/clinical curriculum breakdown and a full list of secondary clinical-partner sites were not published by the Faculty at the level of detail needed to state here with confidence.
universities.hostelOverview: University dormitory places in Novi Sad are state-subsidized and generally reserved for Serbian students or those covered by a specific inter-state agreement; the university's own guidance directs most international students toward private rental housing near the Faculty, with the Faculty's International Department and Erasmus Student Network volunteers available to help with the search.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published for international Medicine students. Food costs should be planned as part of an independent living-cost budget alongside private accommodation.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. International applicants can direct queries to the Faculty's dedicated Studies in English contact for day-to-day support.
universities.studentSupport: International admissions and enrollment run through a dedicated Studies in English contact (medns.studiesinenglish@mf.uns.ac.rs). The Faculty's International Department and Erasmus Student Network volunteers support incoming students with settling in and finding private housing.

faq.question: Is the Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. It is an integrated first- and second-level studies programme -- admission follows directly from completed secondary education, with no separate bachelor's stage required first.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the academic title Doctor of Medicine (MD).

faq.question: How long is the programme and how is it structured?
faq.answer: Six years (360 ECTS credits), taught entirely in English, with clinical training run through the Clinical Center of Vojvodina.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 7,000 per year for the 2026/27 cohort, which includes tuition, online library resources and electronic textbook access. A first installment of at least EUR 1,750 (25% of the total) is due at registration, non-refundable after the enrollment deadline.

faq.question: Are there additional fees besides tuition?
faq.answer: Yes -- a non-refundable EUR 55 application fee, a RSD 5,500 registration fee, and an optional (non-mandatory) Biology or Chemistry preparatory course at EUR 600 per subject.

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: A mandatory Biology and Chemistry entrance exam, held online or on-site by prior arrangement. Applicants without an English-proficiency certificate also sit a university English-language test. There is no standardized-test-based alternative admission route.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and what are the 2026/27 deadlines?
faq.answer: The confirmed 2026/27 cycle is the September intake term: application deadline 4 September 2026, entrance exam 8 September 2026, admitted-candidates list by 10 September, and registration with first-installment payment due by 17 September 2026.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available for international students?
faq.answer: University dormitory places are generally reserved for Serbian students or those covered by a specific inter-state agreement. Most international students arrange private rental housing, with support from the Faculty's International Department and Erasmus Student Network volunteers.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

fee.notes: Officially published 2026/27 tuition: EUR 7,000/year, which includes tuition fees, online library resources and electronic textbook access, per the Faculty's current Admission page. First installment (minimum EUR 1,750, i.e. 25% of the total) is due at registration and is non-refundable after the enrollment deadline. Total is calculated as the annual figure times 6 years -- not published as a lump sum. Separate fees: EUR 55 non-refundable application fee, RSD 5,500 registration fee, optional EUR 600-per-subject preparatory course. An older, stale cached Faculty page still shows a lower EUR 5,500 figure from the 2021/22 cycle; the current Admission page (7,000 EUR) is treated as authoritative.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants who have completed secondary education (general or medical secondary school, or A-levels/12th grade for UK-system applicants)
restrictions: Admission requires the Faculty's own mandatory Biology and Chemistry entrance exam -- no standardized-test-based alternative route is offered
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: English proficiency must be shown via a certificate (e.g. IELTS, TOEFL) or, absent one, a university English-language test taken alongside the entrance exam; native English speakers or those schooled in English are exempt.

admissionsContent.overview: Applicants submit an Application Form and secondary-school documents by email to the Faculty's Studies in English contact, pay the application fee, sit the Biology and Chemistry entrance exam (plus an English test if needed), and if admitted, confirm their seat with a first tuition installment before the registration deadline.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires completed secondary education, English-language proficiency (certificate or in-house test), and a passing result on the Faculty's own Biology and Chemistry entrance exam.
items: Secondary-school completion certificate/diploma with transcripts, in original language plus Serbian translation
English-language proficiency certificate, or an in-house English test taken with the entrance exam if no certificate is held
Mandatory Biology and Chemistry entrance exam, held online or on-site by prior arrangement
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from the university's own admission process

applicationSteps: Submit the Application Form and secondary-school certificates (original language plus Serbian translation) by email to medns.studiesinenglish@mf.uns.ac.rs
Pay the non-refundable EUR 55 (or RSD 6,600) application fee before the entrance exam
Sit the Biology and Chemistry entrance exam (plus English test if required) on the scheduled date
Check the admitted-candidates list, published within about two days of the exam
Confirm the seat by the registration deadline: pay the minimum EUR 1,750 first tuition installment and submit registration documents
